research_question: Does adding an independent conjugate branch to complex convolutions close the real-CNN performance gap as the receive-array size grows?
primary_claim: The missing anti-linear branch W_conj*conj(z), rather than complex representation alone, explains a material part of the Rx16 real-CNN advantage.
falsification_criteria: The widely-linear receiver remains close to the standard complex receiver and materially behind the real CNN at Rx16.
Any apparent gain is explained by unequal semantic inputs, real-parameter count, streaming samples, optimization budget, checkpoint selection, or evaluation samples.
decision_rule: Advance the widely-linear backbone only if it recovers at least half of the standard-complex-to-real-CNN gap at Rx16 in the reliable BLER region without a material Rx2 regression. Otherwise investigate complex activations, normalization, or early antenna compression.

dataset.training_mode: streaming: every epoch generates new frames

methods.convolution: unconstrained real convolution on stacked real/imaginary channels

intentional_differences: Only the convolution family and automatically resolved widths differ.
All three methods are matched to the standard complex receiver's real-parameter budget within 0.1 percent.
